children: U.S. crude oil inventories were down for a fifth consecutive week, while distillate stocks fell to their lowest level in more than two decades, according to data released Wednesday by the U.S. Energy Information Administration.

Commercial crude oil stocks excluding the Strategic Petroleum Reserve fell by 865,000 barrels to 409.8 million barrels in the week ended Oct. 30 and were 4% below the five-year average for the time of year, the EIA said. Crude stocks were expected to have slipped by 200,000 barrels, according to a Wall Street Journal survey of analysts.
Oil stored in the SPR fell by 399,000 barrels to 282.2 million barrels. Oil stocks at Cushing, Okla., the Nymex delivery hub, increased by 280,000 barrels to 27.3 million barrels.

The EIA estimated U.S. crude oil production at 14 million barrels a day, up by 11,000 barrels a day from the previous week. Crude oil imports held steady at 6.4 million barrels a day, while exports fell by 1.2 million barrels a day to 3.7 million barrels a day.

Refinery capacity use rose to 94.5% from 92.8% the week before, with crude input to refineries up by 199,000 barrels a day to 16.7 million barrels a day. Refinery runs were forecast at 92.9% in the Journal survey.

Gasoline inventories declined by 222,000 barrels to 209 million barrels, and were 2% below the five-year average, the EIA said. Gasoline demand rose by 450,000 barrels a day to 8.8 million barrels a day. Gasoline stocks were expected to be have risen by 200,000 barrels.

Distillate fuel stocks fell by 3.6 million barrels to 99.3 million barrels, their lowest level since May of 2003 and 13% below the five-year average. Distillate stocks were expected to have fallen by 1 million barrels.
